Enable data-driven decision-making Our Machine Learning algorithms create accurate predictions and detect deviations from optimal procedures. FAQ Can Assaia's solutions work with our own cameras? Yes, our system can be used with a wide range of cameras that are already installed at airports around the world. Does the system work in snow, rain, or fog? Yes! Our system has been trialed many times in areas where we saw a lot of snow, rain, fog, or sandstorms. In most instances, the system did stay within normal performance levels. How does the system perform during the night? The performance during the night is often even slightly better due to more constant light sources on the apron.As a rule of thumb, our system can work in any condition where a human being with healthy eyes can see the turnaround. Is the solution GDPR compliant? Yes, our solution is fully General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) compliant. It has been used within many jurisdictions throughout the world, including Europe, where we were able to get the acknowledgment from multiple data security departments of airports and airlines. Can the system be used to detect FOD? The system can detect many objects on an aircraft stand and determine if the stand is clear for an aircraft to enter. It can also support the process of FOD check and determine whether it was performed properly. Does the system have to be calibrated for every stand? Not necessarily. If the camera position and the layout of the aircraft stand are almost identical, it is sufficient to calibrate the system once for these stands. Can the system be installed on-premise as well? Yes, it runs in the cloud and on-premise. Can we observe multiple stands with one camera? Yes, one camera can cover multiple stands in some layouts, provided the angle, field of view and resolution are sufficient. In some cases detections may be limited, so additional cameras may still be recommended for broader event coverage. Does the system work with PTZ cameras? Assaia can work with PTZ cameras if it is used as a fixed camera. Active PTZ movement, preset changes, auto-tracking, or other features that change the view are not suitable, because the scene must remain stable. What is Predicted Off-Block Time (POBT)? Predicted Off-Block Time (POBT)is an AI-powered forecast of when an aircraft will push back or leave its parking stand. By combining real-time turnaround milestones, historical operational patterns, and live external data feeds (such as weather and airspace constraints), POBT provides a more dynamic and accurate departure forecast than traditional static schedules. What is the minimum camera resolution required? The smaller the objects and the more subtle the events the system needs to detect, the higher the resolution of the camera should be. What is the ideal camera position? There is no single ideal camera position for every stand. In general, we prefer a fixed, stable camera mounted at the height of 15-20 meters and angled appropriately to minimise obstructions and clearly cover the aircraft and stand. Ideal positioning depends on the availability of the existing positions for mounting, expected event coverage scope and expected aircraft types. For stand optimization during heavy snowfall, should we rely on Predicted Ready Time (PRDT) or Predicted Off-Block Time (POBT)? Assaia recommends using Predicted Ready Time (PRDT) as your core foundation during heavy snowfall.
Stand allocation and sequencing decisions are rooted directly on the stand itself. As PRDT measures turnaround milestones with high precision, it offers the clearest, most controllable baseline for managing stand capacity under operational stress.
Crucially during winter operations, on-stand de-icing falls directly within Assaia's computer vision tracking. PRDT automatically accounts for de-icing progress, incorporating one of the largest winter variables directly into your ready signal.
While PRDT gives you the baseline for stand availability, Predicted Off-Block Time (POBT) serves as a complementary second layer - helping teams anticipate external departure delays and predict exactly when the stand will physically clear. Does the system work with our existing VMS? We have already worked with many VMSs in the past and our system can easily integrate with all the major VMS providers. Can we use multiple cameras for the same location? Our system can work with multiple cameras covering the same location/aircraft stand. Our existing customer installations normally use one to three cameras per stand. It is also common to install cameras in Passenger Boarding Bridges to detect boarding-specific events. Do Predicted Ready Time (PRDT) and Predicted Off-Block Time (POBT) differ in practice? Yes, Predicted Ready Time (PRDT) and Predicted Off-Block Time (POBT) regularly differ by more than 5 minutes in real-world operations.
While PRDT and POBT are closely related - since "ground handling complete" generally means ready for pushback - they measure two different stages of aircraft departure:
- PRDT is Assaia's on-stand signal. Powered by direct computer vision monitoring, it accurately predicts the exact moment all turnaround activities are completed and the aircraft is physically ready.
- POBT is our airside movement predictor. It takes the PRDT ready signal and incorporates external operational factors outside the stand to estimate when the aircraft can actually vacate the stand.
As an aircraft can be ready at the stand but held up by factors like taxiway congestion, departure slot constraints, adjacent stand pushback conflicts, or runway closures, a flight may achieve PRDT at 10:00 while POBT estimates departure at 10:05 or later. Turnaround Control has already proven its ability to improve turnaround operations at airports like: This is some text inside of a div block. $30m in savings reduced  taxi-in time Reduced  operational costs Requirements Air Canada required full situational awareness of the turnaround process to reduce turnaround times and improve resilience while decreasing delays for its passengers. They needed real-time visibility of all turnaround events to provide a single source of truth for their turnaround managers. This ensured on-time performance while maintaining safety standards and reducing their environmental impact. Toronto Pearson International Airport provided access to Assaia’s TurnaroundControl solution to help the airline reduce delays, minimize ground time, and maximize gate capacity utilization. Solution Assaia's TurnaroundControl uses a combination of AI and computer vision to track exactly what happens during aircraft turnaround in real-time. The resulting data highlights when turnaround subprocesses (like fueling or catering) are falling behind schedule. As a result, mitigative action can be taken immediately to minimize delays and increase gate availability. Deviations from schedule and predicted delays are communicated to users via TurnaroundControl’s alerting capability. This reduces alert fatigue amongst teams, allowing users to rely on the solution to flag delays, focusing their efforts on particular flights rather than monitoring all ongoing departures constantly. This method of management by exception means Air Canada can manage more flights with the same number of staff. During an initial usage period of three months, a subset of all flights were actively managed via Assaia’s TurnaroundControl solution with turnaround managers observing and responding to alerts as they came in. Real-time information about turnaround issues and delays were previously not available.  Now, turnaround managers can respond more efficiently and minimize the effect of these issues on the on-time performance of the flight. The measured benefit, an average 3.4 minutes reduction in ground delays, represents massive savings for the airline.
